title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the next page, §8.1): X is smooth, proper and connected of dimension n over a perfect field k of characteristic p. W = W(k), H^i(X) is crystalline cohomology, assumed to be a 'good theory' with H_DR(X) = H(X) ⊗^L_W k. From this one gets the universal-coefficient sequences 0 → H^i(X)⊗_W k → H^i_DR(X) → Tor_1^W(H^{i+1}(X),k) = _pTors^{i+1}(X) → 0. The surrounding section is a heuristic count of the Frobenius eigenvalues on vanishing cohomology that are p-adic units. This NB (8.4.4) computes the 'unit-root' and 'top-slope' parts in middle degree, with the torsion contributions made explicit.

Two operators are used, as the bottom note and the next page's margin define them:
- F = F_X^*, a σ-linear map. The subscript ss means the F-semisimple (stable, Fitting) part.
- V = σ^{-1}F_{X*}, the trace/push-forward along absolute Frobenius, a σ^{-1}-linear map with VF = p^n. The superscript ss means the V-semisimple part.
For a p^{±1}-linear endomorphism of a finite-length module over a perfect field, the functor M ↦ M_ss is exact (Fitting decomposition). Moreover, if F is nilpotent on _pT then it is nilpotent on T, and hence on T⊗k.

(a) The F side.
- F_X^* kills Ω^j for j ≥ 1. So F on H^i_DR factors as H^i_DR → H^i(X,O_X) → H^i_DR, using the complex map O_X → F_*Ω^·, f ↦ f^p.
- Hence F is nilpotent on H^i_DR for i > n. It is therefore nilpotent on the sub H^i⊗k and the quotient _pTors^{i+1}, and so on Tors^i⊗k and _pTors^i for i > n.
- Since F = b∘a while F on H^n(O_X) is a∘b, their stable parts agree: (H^n_DR)_ss ≅ H^n(X,O_X)_ss.
- The term _pTors^{n+1} has nilpotent F, so this equals (H^n(X)⊗k)_ss.
- Tensoring 0 → Tors^n → H^n → H^n_lib → 0 with k is exact because H^n_lib is free. Taking ss parts gives
(*) 0 → (Tors^n(X)⊗k)_ss → H^n(X,O_X)_ss → (H^n_lib(X)⊗k)_ss → 0.
So the stable rank of Hasse–Witt on H^n(O_X) equals the number of slope-0 eigenvalues on H^n plus a torsion correction.

(b) The V side, dually.
- The Cartier operator gives a complex map F_*Ω^· → Ω^n[-n], since C kills exact n-forms. So V on H^i_DR factors through H^{i-n}(X,Ω^n).
- Hence V is nilpotent for i < n, and therefore on Tors^i⊗k and _pTors^i for i ≤ n (the latter via the surjection H^{i-1}_DR → _pTors^i).
- For i = n, (H^n_DR)^ss ≅ H^0(X,Ω^n)^ss.
- The UCT sequence for i = n, together with the V-nilpotence of Tors^n⊗k, gives
(**) 0 → (H^n_lib⊗k)^ss → H^0(X,Ω^n)^ss → (_pTors^{n+1}(X))^ss → 0.
This counts slope-n eigenvalues via the stable rank of Cartier on H^0(Ω^n).

Final remark: (*) and (**) should be 'transposes' of each other. Under Serre duality, H^n(O_X) is dual to H^0(Ω^n) with F dual to Cartier. Under crystalline Poincaré duality, H^n_lib is self-dual with F ↔ V, and the torsion pairing makes Tors^n dual to Tors^{n+1}, so Tors^n⊗k is dual to _pTors^{n+1}. The next page laments that Poincaré duality is not yet available, which dates the page around 1970–71 (Berthelot's theory in progress, 'p≠2'), not 1958.
errors: Not an error, but a precondition: V must act integrally on crystalline cohomology compatibly with the Cartier-defined action on H_DR. Grothendieck implicitly uses V = σ^{-1}F_{X*} (Gysin/trace), so VF = p^n, not p. This needs Gysin maps and the compatibility of the UCT sequences with them, which were not yet established.

In (a) the line 'Tor_1^W(H^i(X),k) ≃ _pTors^i(X)' is correct. However, F-nilpotence on _pTors^{n+1} (needed for (*)) follows from nilpotence on Tors^{n+1}⊗k, not directly from H^n_DR. The page passes over this silently.

The claim that (*) and (**) are transposes presupposes integral crystalline Poincaré duality, including the torsion linking Tors^i ↔ Tors^{2n+1-i}. Grothendieck flags this himself ('Sans doute'); it was later supplied by Berthelot (1974).
Dating: the archive date '[à partir de 1958]' is misleading. The content (Berthelot's crystalline cohomology, p≠2) points to c. 1970–71.

ideas.what: Frobenius on de Rham cohomology factors through H^i(X,O_X); hence the F-stable part of H^i_DR equals the Hasse–Witt stable part of H^i(O_X), and F is nilpotent on H^i_DR for i>n.
ideas.modern_name: Factorization of Frobenius through the Hodge quotient / Hasse–Witt stable part
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hasse–Witt, Serre, Cartier); in crystalline form Mazur (1972–73), Katz
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1970/74); unsure

ideas.what: Dually, V (trace of Frobenius) on de Rham cohomology factors through H^{i-n}(X,Ω^n) via the Cartier operator.
ideas.modern_name: Cartier operator / V on de Rham and crystalline cohomology; Mazur–Ogus 'Frobenius and the Hodge filtration'

ideas.what: Exact sequence (*) relating the Hasse–Witt stable part of H^n(O_X) to the unit-root part of free crystalline H^n plus the F-stable part of Tors^n⊗k.
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root / p-rank formula with torsion correction (cf. H^i(X,O_X)_ss ≅ H^i_et(X,F_p)⊗k and slope-0 part of H^i(X,WO_X))

ideas.what: Dual sequence (**) for the slope-n part via the Cartier-stable part of H^0(Ω^n), with the conjecture that (*) and (**) are Poincaré/Serre-dual transposes (torsion linking Tors^n ↔ Tors^{n+1}).
ideas.modern_name: Duality of slope-0 and slope-n parts; crystalline Poincaré duality with torsion linking (Berthelot; Ekedahl's duality for de Rham–Witt)

missed.claim: This NB serves Grothendieck's heuristic (§8) counting unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues in the vanishing cohomology of hyperplane sections. The bookkeeping explicitly tracks how crystalline torsion enters Hasse–Witt stable ranks. That is a precursor of later questions on ordinarity of generic hyperplane sections and complete intersections (Deligne, Illusie 'Ordinarité des intersections complètes générales'). The page itself contains only known-type material.
missed.quote: Sans doute (*) et (**) sont transposés l'un de l'autre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck around 1970 doing slope/torsion bookkeeping (F vs V stable parts, torsion linking) before the de Rham–Witt and duality theory that made it rigorous.

deep.surprise_reason: The sequences are correct and natural consequences of the universal-coefficient formula, the factorization of F/V through H^n(O)/H^0(Ω^n), and exactness of semisimple parts. They are now standard (Illusie, Ekedahl, Berthelot). The interest is historical: an early, explicit torsion-aware formulation, with the duality correctly anticipated.
transcription_corrections: In (*), the first term reads (Tors^n(X)⊗k)_ss; the lower index on Tors is 'n', with the scribble likely a correction.
In (**), 'ss' appears as superscripts (V-semisimple), with an additional 'ss' written under the arrows; these are likely under-arrow annotations rather than double indices.
(**) is followed by '→ 0' (written '+0' / 'Toz' in the image), and the 'ss' under that arrow belongs to _pTors^{n+1}(X)^ss.

The bottom line should read roughly: 'Notation: l'indice ss indique la partie semi-simple pour F, l'exposant ss ___ [pour V]'. This is consistent with the next page's margin (index ss for F_X = F_X^*, exponent ss for V_X = σ^{-1}F_{X*}).
In b), the text reads 'V opérant sur H^i(X)⊗_W k pour i<n est nilpotent, et aussi opère [nilpotent] sur Tors^i(X)⊗_W k et _pTors^i(X) pour i ≤ n' (with 'i ≤ n' double-underlined).
